subject: Add and use has_ended helper testing if a Sanction is expired
message:
Add and use has_ended helper testing if a Sanction is expired

This helper is mostly used in places where we infer a topic assignment
(is this entity currently sanctioned or debarred?) from the end date.

In a few places, this commit also changes what "now" date is used as a
comparison. In the helper, we use settings.RUN_TIME. This is more
consistent than using datetime.now() (used in a couple places), which
changes throughout the run. It is more semantically correct than using
context.data_time, as our topic assignments should reflect whether an
entity is debarred *now* (for some definition of now) rather than
at the time when the data was published.

subject: Make it an is_active helper instead

b) also cover the edgecase of a sanction that begins in the future

subject: Allow validating the number of property manifestation for a type
message:
Allow validating the number of property manifestation for a type

In the metadata YAML, an assertion specification like this means that at 10 Person entities have at least one birthPlace property value.

min:
  property_values:
    Person:
      birthPlace: 10

This carries a slight ambiguity with regards to inheritance: Can an
assertion on LegalEntity.country be satisfied by Person and Company
entities? At the moment, the implementation does not allow this.

This adds a new section to statistics.json which looks like this:

	"things": {
	    "total": 698,
	    [...]
	    "property_values": [
	      {
		"schema": "Company",
		"property": "address",
		"count": 207
	      },
	      {
		"schema": "Company",
		"property": "country",
		"count": 199
	      },
	      {
		"schema": "Company",
		"property": "name",
		"count": 202
	      },
	      {
		"schema": "Company",
		"property": "sector",
		"count": 201
	      },

		"schema": "Company",
		"property": "taxNumber",
		"count": 199
	      },

		"count": 199
	      },

zavod/tests/test_dedupe.py::test_resolver_tools would fail because
test_issue_logger does not clean up its context. In CI, another test
would run in between, calling clear_contextvars and thereby cleaning up.

The previous change restores the contextvars to what they were before
context.begin() was called, so this failure to clean up now gets
propagated.

subject: Fix and test log redaction of env vars in issues.json (and Sentry)
message:
Fix and test log redaction of env vars in issues.json (and Sentry)

The issue was that in the processor chain, the two emitting processors
`log_isue` and `sentry_processor` were inserted before the redactor. The
consequence was that the redaction would work for the command line, but
unredacted log messages would be sent to `issues.json` and Sentry.

As far as I can tell, this bug has been present since the initial
introduction of this feature in
https://github.com/opensanctions/opensanctions/commit/8bf3ed700459d0abf867f27366c3ee17df3d48fd
on 2024-05-10.

This fixes https://github.com/opensanctions/operations/issues/1086.

[logs] Fix logging to issues

The issue was that format_json would move level -> severity in the event
dict and subsequently let issues_log error out.

The comment in there about any of these processors performing
stringifcation (which made me not touch it previously) is a lie. Non-str
objects in the log dict simply won't be redacted. This commit doesn't
fix that, but doesn't change it either

I feel this thing is up for a bit of a refactor. Some of the stuff in
there (like the database URI redaction) is a bit scary.

subject: [ru_egrul] Ingest all archives to build historic Ownership/Directoship (#1815)
message:
[ru_egrul] Ingest all archives to build historic Ownership/Directoship (#1815)

See https://github.com/opensanctions/opensanctions/issues/847

The general idea is: We parse all the daily zips into a dataframe (which we save locally as a parquet to be able to resume, but this is more of a convenience thing). We take 2022-01-01 as a base and subsequently update it with the companies from the daily updates. (Actually, we first create monthly partial packages, merge these into a yearly, then fold that into the full cause it's faster than doing 365 joins on the full dataset) Updating means just using the new version of the company, but keeping the no-longer-present Ownership and Directorship relations around and setting and end_date on them.

At the end, we write it all out to CSV, which is then ingested by the crawler in zavod.

subject: [us_tn_med_exclusions] Switch to zyte with geolocation US
message:
[us_tn_med_exclusions] Switch to zyte with geolocation US

They're doing DNS-based geofencing, which I haven't seen before. I
haven't fully understood what is happening. When connecting to a VPN in
the US, I can resolve www.tn.gov fine, but I get different opinions:

```
$ dig a www.tn.gov @1.1.1.1 +short
www.extglb.tn.gov.
170.141.165.146

$ dig a www.tn.gov @8.8.8.8 +short
198.18.1.187
```

Doing the same from Europe:

```
$ dig a www.tn.gov @8.8.8.8
[...]
; OPT=15: 00 17 4e 6f 20 72 65 73 70 6f 6e 73 65 20 72 65 63 65 69 76 65 64 20 66 72 6f 6d 20 6e 61 6d 65 20 73 65 72 76 65 72 73 20 66 6f 72 20 65 78 74 67 6c 62 2e 74 6e 2e 67 6f 76 ("..No response received from name servers for extglb.tn.gov")
```

Using a DNS resolver in the US from Europe:

```
$ dig a www.tn.gov @88.198.92.222
[...]
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: SERVFAIL, id: 61346
[...]
;; QUESTION SECTION:
;www.tn.gov.			IN	A

;; ANSWER SECTION:
www.tn.gov.		270	IN	CNAME	www.extglb.tn.gov.
```

Weirdly enough, using 88.198.92.222, which I think is in the US and not
an Anycast IP, I get differen results looking up www.extglb.tn.gov. from
Europe vs. US, which is... weird? DNS does not have a Referrer header,
right?

Anyway, this fixes it. Happy for any thoughts.

subject: [wd_categories] Emit entities without topics as external
message:
[wd_categories] Emit entities without topics as external

Some categories we crawl but don't assign topics to. We do this for two reasons:

1. We only want to discover interesting positions in the category (which
   then trigger at topic assignment), but there are more persons in the
   category not relevant to us.
2. We want to discover QIDs for enrichment, just in case the Wikidata
   enricher (which only searches for a single name) doesn't find
   them. In this case, the xref process will discover the QID for the
   cluster (but not actually pull in the statements marked as external).

In both cases, we want to emit the statements as external.

subject: Don't backfill issues log
message:
Don't backfill issues log

I don't know why this was ever a thing, but this breaks the reasonable assumption that the issues log contains the issues from "this run". For collections, this currently means that `issues.log` is append-only and forever. Leaf datasets currently have their issues log cleared by `Context.begin(clear=True)`.

If I understand the mechanics of this correctly, this means that collections will now export and `issues.log` containing issues logged during the export stage, i.e. validation and assembly.

https://github.com/opensanctions/opensanctions/pull/3362

Recapping the conversation for any future archaeologists:

From @pudo:

> I think the premise back when I built it was that you'd be able to run zavod export without running zavod crawl before, and it would just backfill everything. Since this has never happened, let's just jettison the use case! Would you have one look around the code to see if there's other stuff we can not backfill, like resources.json, index.json etc.? resources probably only after the other successful run stuff is merged?

from @leonhandreke:

> I thought about this some more. I feel like your idea of making the steps independent and always backfill is really nice and maybe we should hold onto it?
>
> I think the core issue may be that we don't have a "lifecycle orchestrator". Context is too short-lived, and cli is... well, at least it should be just a little layer on top of the business logic. We want to reset the issues at the beginning of the "dataset lifecycle", but that beginning is crawl for leaves, and export for collections.
>
> Anyway, I feel like this is an okay fix for now until we figure out a more appropriate strategy, so I'll merge.

subject: assertions: refactor to dumb down a bit (#3419)
message:
assertions: refactor to dumb down a bit (#3419)

Refactor to dumb the whole thing down a bit. Disadvantage is we no longer get Dataset parse level validation for whether the format of the assertions is correct - we'll only know when the validator runs. But now assertions can have quite different config formats (some take just a value, some a value per country, some a value per schema/prop combo) and it won't be two layers of indirection anymore. That also made the error messages a bit better.

Also, make the assertions unit tests a bit mroe unit-testy. Previously, they relied on fat fixtures (`testdatasetN` that made it intransparent what was actually going on and hard to change these fixtures without breaking tests.

See https://github.com/opensanctions/opensanctions/issues/3359

subject: cli: Shell completions for dataset paths
message:
cli: Shell completions for dataset paths

Activate shell completions by putting the following in your zsh .envrc. This magic will cache the completion function for 30 days to now slow shell startup down

```
(){ [[ $# -gt 0 ]] || _ZAVOD_COMPLETE=zsh_source zavod > .zavod-complete.zsh; source .zavod-complete.zsh; } .zavod-complete.zsh(Nm-30)
```

Alternatively, the slow way that does not cache is

```
eval "$(_ZAVOD_COMPLETE=zsh_source zavod)"
```

subject: statistics: Add total and fill_rate to entities_with_prop, fold fill rate assertions into StatisticsAssertionsValidator
message:
statistics: Add total and fill_rate to entities_with_prop, fold fill rate assertions into StatisticsAssertionsValidator

The `entities_with_prop` facets in statistics.json now include `total`
(entity count for that schema) and `fill_rate` (count/total) alongside
the existing `count` field.

This lets `check_assertion` handle `property_fill_rate` directly from
the statistics dict, so `PropertyFillRateAssertionsValidator` — which
was doing its own per-entity counting pass — can be removed.

subject: Modularize CLAUDE.md into routing layer + crawler skills
message:
Modularize CLAUDE.md into routing layer + crawler skills

Restructure crawler documentation into a modular skill system:
- Root CLAUDE.md: slim routing layer pointing to skills and guide
- .claude/docs/crawler-guide.md: shared crawler patterns (YAML template,
    helpers, lookups, FTM schemata, qsv analysis, code style)
- .claude/skills/crawler-pep/: PEP-specific skill with examples
- .claude/skills/crawler-sanctions/: sanctions-specific skill with examples

Key design decisions:
- Skills reference a shared guide to avoid duplication
- Code examples live in separate examples.md files per Anthropic's
recommendation (SKILL.md under 500 lines, progressive disclosure)
- Skills accept GitHub issue URLs in addition to data source URLs
- Guide includes Zyte API stop-and-warn, SPA API discovery tips,
    audit_data anti-patterns, and file creation boundaries

* [fr_tresor_gels_avoir] Fix identification segment and address lookup warnings

fr_tresor_gels_avoir crawler:

  "République de Biélorussie" → BY so the auto-parser can accept these

- identification_segment: add entries for fax numbers (Télécopieur),
  proprietary IDs (Cedar Rose, Acuris, SAM, EDI), KPP codes, registration
  locations (Etablissement principal, Lieu d'enregistrement variants),
  associated persons/entities, LEI codes, VAT, legal forms, multi-value
  registration numbers, multiple dates, and complex mixed-property segments
- identification_full: add match for "Numéro de registre économique (CBLS)"
  to prevent a false split caused by the OMI TEXT_KEY matching inside
  "économique"
- addresses: add 4 new multi-address splits for Russian, Belarusian, Belize,
